SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
S.I. Special Branch **〔此处转录不清〕**
REPORT
Date December 1, 1937
Subject. Circular letter of a Shanghai Youth Mobile Propaganda
Group distributed among Chinese residents in the
International Settlement.
Made by J.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

With reference to the remarks of D.C. (Special Branch)
on the attached report: I beg to state that the members of
the Shanghai Youth Mobile Propaganda Group, when delivering
letters as a rule, leave no address, merely expressing a
willingness to return at some other time for such contribution
as the recipient is desirous of giving, but which he is unable
to produce at the time of application.

8 copies of a handbill purporting to emanate from the
Shanghai Youth Mobile Propaganda Group (上海青年流動宣傳團),
were found on the pavement outside the Wing On Company's
premises on Nanking Road near Chekiang Road at 7 p.m. November
30, 1937. A copy of this pamphlet is attached to this report
with translation.

The address of this Group at House No. 31 Lane 88, Yung
An Road, Rue Villot is still being maintained, although observers
fail to notice any activity on the premises. Inquiries are
still proceeding with a view to obtaining further information
on the matter.

Sih Tse-liang
C. D. I.

Copy to Mr Smith.
Sih
3/12
CP
D.C. (Special Branch).
mB

1937年11月30日晚7时，在南京路近浙江路的永安公司（Wing On Company）门外人行道上，发现8份据称出自上海青年流动宣传团（上海青年流動宣傳團）的传单。本报告的附件中包含该传单的副本及译文。

该团体位于米罗路（Rue Villot）永安里88弄31号的地址目前仍在使用，尽管观察人员未注意到该处有任何活动。调查仍在进行中，以获取有关此事的进一步信息。

pages.en:
Translation of a pamphlet purporting to emanate from the
Shanghai Youth Mobile Propaganda Group, copies of which
were found on Liang Yuod near Chinkiang Road on 29.11.37

A letter to the Chinese Citizens

It is two weeks since Shanghai fell into the hands of
the enemy. During this period, we have come to realise the
bitter truth of homelessness. We have been forced to leave
Shanghai, a place of embarrassment for all, and find places
to shelter but inadequate. Before mid-day road-move to you,
we wish to give you the following advice:-
From a military point of view, the withdrawal of the
Chinese troop from Shanghai is a strategic retreat. Japan
despatched five batches of reinforcements to Shanghai and
launched six successive general offensives before they
occupied this area. What they obtain now is only a piece of
devastated land with all houses thoroughly destroyed by
fire. We have made Japan pay more than was our valuation of
this piece of land.
The present protracted hostilities is exhausting
the strength of the enemy. The weaker country (China) will
lose more men while the stronger will have to defray a far
greater expense in the war. If we can hold the war for six
months, we will bring about a collapse in the economic system
of Japan. Should the war last for one year, we do not know
where Japan will be: the final victory would then be ours.
After the withdrawal of Chinese troops from Shanghai,
the enemy, backed by their military power, put forth a number
of harsh demands to threaten and embarrass the authorities
of the Special Districts and compel them to suppress anti-
Japanese speeches and writings. At the same time, they made
use of the newspapers in Shanghai to spread propaganda with
the object of discouraging the war spirit of the Chinese
people here. Do you believe that Chinese troops, while being
able to hold out for three months in Shanghai, where no per-
manent defensive works had been constructed, would be unable
to make a stand at Chingyankiang and Soochow for a few days?
The propaganda unleashed by traitors has indeed shattered
the faith of a part of the people in the present war.
We wish to give you a little true information. Chinese
troops are at present still fighting the enemy in the vicinity
of Chingyankiang. Ten thousand enemy troops have been killed
and a large number captured. The reports in the newspapers
are not true and you should not be deceived by them.
This war is a war for the emancipation of our race, in
which the people should all participate. We shall not be
ashamed nor discouraged at the changes in the military
situation. We should do our duty during this critical period.
Abyssinia was defeated because her people were not
well organized and failed to support their government. We
should not commit the same mistake. Nationals, rise up!
Beat down the only enemy we have - Imperialistic Japan.

SHANGHAI YOUTH MOBILE PROPAGANDA GROUP.
pages.zh:
据称出自上海青年流动宣传团的传单译文，该传单副本于1937年11月29日在镇江路附近的良友（Liang Yuod，原文如此）被发现

致中国同胞书

上海沦入敌手已两周。在此期间，我们深切体会到无家可归的悲惨真相。我们被迫离开令所有人蒙羞的上海，寻找栖身之所，却难以得到 adequate（充足）的安置。在中午之前移步至贵处之际，我们谨提出以下建议：-
从军事角度来看，中国军队从上海撤退是战略性的转移。日本向上海派遣了五批增援部队，并发动了六次连续的大规模进攻，才占领了这一地区。他们现在得到的只是一片废墟，所有房屋均被大火彻底摧毁。我们让日本付出的代价，超过了我们对这片土地的估值。
目前的持久战正在消耗敌人的力量。弱国（中国）会损失更多的人员，而强国则必须承担更巨大的战争开支。如果我们能将战争维持六个月，我们将导致日本经济体系的崩溃。如果战争持续一年，日本将不知置身何处：最终的胜利将属于我们。
中国军队从上海撤退后，敌人依仗其军事力量，提出了一系列苛刻要求，以威胁和为难特区当局，迫使他们压制反日言论和文字。同时，他们利用上海的报纸进行宣传，旨在打击此地中国人的抗战精神。你们是否相信，中国军队能够在没有修建永久防御工事的上海坚守三个月，却无法在镇江和苏州坚守几天？
汉奸散布的宣传确实动摇了部分民众对当前战争的信心。
我们希望向你们提供一些真实的信息。中国军队目前仍在镇江附近与敌人作战。敌军已被击毙一万人，另有大量被俘。报纸上的报道并不属实，你们不应受其欺骗。
这场战争是我们民族解放的战争，全体人民都应参与其中。我们不应因军事局势的变化而感到羞愧或气馁。在这个危急时刻，我们应恪尽职守。
阿比西尼亚之所以战败，是因为其人民组织不善，未能支持政府。我们不应重蹈覆辙。同胞们，奋起吧！
打倒我们唯一的敌人——帝国主义日本。

上海青年流动宣传团。

INCIDENTS OCCURRING IN LOUZA DISTRICT
DUE TO SINO-JAPANESE HOSTILITIES

At 0.00 a.m. 29-11-37 Plain Clothes J.P.C.s 3209
and 3110 proceeded to the section from Peking Road near
No. 10 Wong, four male Chinese

(1) Tsang Ah Mui (曾阿美), 22, Kompo, S/unemp.
R.F.A.
(2) Lee Sun Kai (李生記), 24, Kompo, S/unemp.
R.F.A.
(3) Lam Ah Lung (林亞龍), 10, Kompo, S/unemp.
R.F.A.
(4) Ts'ung Hing (朱興), 22, Kompo, S/unemp.R.F.A.

who were in possession and attempting to sell a small
quantity of brass piping, value about 70 cents which
they, the J.P.C.s, suspected them of having stolen.

On enquiries being made by J.D.J. 275 and D.S.
Nicoll, the four suspects stated that they had not
actually stolen the property in question, but that at
about 7.a.m. 29-11-37 it had been stolen by another
unknown male Chinese, who, on being challenged by a
C.P.C. No. unknown, had left the property outside the
Teh Sung Li alleyway, North Kiangse Road and made good
his escape.

Detectives visited the scene of the alleged offence
but no information could be obtained which might tend
to either prove or disprove this statement.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. ____
S.I., Special Branch ____
REPORT
Date Nov. 28, 1937.

Subject Circular letter of a Shanghai Youth Mobile Propaganda Group distributed among Chinese residents in the International Settlement.

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by C [签名]

Copies of a printed circular letter were recently distributed by messenger among Chinese residents of the International Settlement, the addresses of those to whom these circular letters were sent being selected from the telephone book. This letter, a specimen of which is appended to this report with translation, declares that members of the Shanghai Youth Mobile Propaganda Group had assisted in the defence of Greater Shanghai, but on the withdrawal of the Chinese armies from Shanghai had been forced to seek refuge in the Settlement. In order to continue the work of national salvation, the letter continues, members have decided to leave Shanghai and the Chinese citizens are requested to contribute to the travelling expenses of the Group.

The origin of this letter is an organization entitled "The Shanghai Youth Mobile Propaganda Group" (上海青年流動宣傳團) with an address at 775 Min Kuo Road and the commander of this Group is one named Pang Lee (彭蠡) who signed and chopped the document.

The Shanghai Youth Propaganda Group was hitherto unknown to this office and enquiries show that while the office on Min Kuo Road, mentioned in the letter is no longer functioning, a secret communication office is now located at House No.31, Lane 38, Yung Hwa Li, Rue Millot, entrance being gained via Boulevard de Montigny.

Discreet enquiries made at this address have failed to confirm the existence of this office, although it is learnt that the occupants of the house in question who moved in on November 7 were persons connected with the Woosung-

CP
D.C. (a)
Copy to Mr Santly & further enquiries re office in Settlement. P.S. People can contribute unless they know where to send money.
（印章：1937 NOV 29 RECEIVED）

报告
日期：1937年11月28日。

事由：上海青年流动宣传团向国际租界中国居民散发的通函。

呈报人：首席侦探督察（C.D.I.）Sih Tse-liang 转呈人：C [签名]

最近，信差向国际租界的中国居民分发了印刷的通函副本，收件人地址是从电话簿中选取的。这封信（样本附于本报告并附有译文）声称，上海青年流动宣传团成员曾协助保卫大上海，但在中国军队从上海撤退后，被迫进入租界避难。信中接着说，为了继续救国工作，成员们决定离开上海，并请中国公民资助该团体的旅费。

这封信的来源是一个名为“上海青年流动宣传团”（上海青年流動宣傳團）的组织，地址位于民国路775号，该团体的指挥官名叫彭蠡（Pang Lee），他在文件上签名并盖章。

本处室此前并不知晓上海青年宣传团的存在，调查显示，信中提到的民国路办事处已不再运作，目前一个秘密通讯处位于米罗路（Rue Millot）永华里38弄31号，入口经由蒙梯尼路（Boulevard de Montigny）进入。

在该地址进行的谨慎调查未能证实该办事处的存在，尽管获悉该房屋的居住者于11月7日搬入，是与吴淞-

（左侧手写批注）：
CP
副总监（a）
抄送桑特利先生（Mr Santly）并进一步查询租界内的办事处。附言：除非人们知道把钱寄到哪里，否则无法捐款。
（印章：1937年11月29日 收讫）
副本已发送给 [签名] 先生 11月29日
特别情报科（S.I.）按指示 11月30日 D.R.

pages.en:
Translation of a printed circular letter
purporting to emanate from the Shanghai Youths'
Mobile Propaganda Group, copies of which were
sent to residents in the International Settlement
by messenger.

----------

While China was waging an extensive war
of resistance during the past three months, we
enlisted a number of youths in Shanghai who rendered
military services as well as conducted propaganda
in Soochow, Kashing, Wooshow and other places with
a view to strengthening the anti-enemy spirit of the
people in the rear.

On November 11, Chinese troops withdrew from
Shanghai with the result that the offices of this
Group (Shanghai Youths' Mobile Propaganda Group),
hitherto situated in Nantao, fell into the hands
of the enemy. Traitorous Chinese in Nantao became
influential and commenced to arrest anti-Japanese
elements in the area. Under the circumstances
we were unable to remain in Nantao and at 2 a.m.
November 12, members of this group withdrew from
the area and entered the foreign concessions by
climbing over the wall of the Ningpo Guild.

At present the enemy is in full command of Shang-
hai and numbers of Chinese people living in this
country have a disinclination for a prolonged war
and are easy prey to the perfidious propaganda of
these traitors. In view of this the members of
this group have decided to leave Shanghai for
inland places to waken the spirit of the people in
the interior.

We have also decided not to carry anything of
an incriminating nature with us on our voyage in
order to avoid interference from the enemy, who are
at present inspecting vessels passing Woosung. We
are not afraid of being killed but we have to take
these precautions against danger. We will sell all
our belongings that are of value and will solicit
contributions from various circles to aid our
travelling expenses. You are enthusiastic and
patriotic and are hereby kindly requested to render
us your generous assistance.

Pang Lee ( 彭 嘉 ), C!
of the Shanghai Youths'
Mobile Propaganda Group.

据称出自上海青年流动宣传团的印刷通函译文，副本由信差发送给国际租界的居民。

---

在过去三个月中国进行大规模抗战期间，我们在上海招募了一批青年，他们在苏州、嘉兴、吴淞等地提供军事服务并进行宣传，旨在加强后方人民的抗敌精神。

11月11日，中国军队从上海撤退，导致本团体（上海青年流动宣传团）此前位于南市的办事处落入敌手。南市的汉奸势力坐大，开始逮捕该地区的反日分子。在这种情况下，我们无法留在南市，本团体成员于11月12日凌晨2时撤离该地区，翻越宁波同乡会的围墙进入外国租界。

目前敌人完全控制上海，居住在此地的许多中国人对持久战缺乏意愿，容易成为这些汉奸背信弃义宣传的猎物。有鉴于此，本团体成员决定离开上海前往内地，以唤醒内地人民的精神。

我们还决定在行程中不携带任何可能招致罪责的物品，以避免受到目前正在检查经过吴淞船只的敌人的干扰。我们不怕牺牲，但必须采取这些预防措施以防危险。我们将变卖所有有价值的财产，并向各界募捐以资助我们的旅费。诸位热情爱国，特此恳请给予慷慨援助。

彭嘉（Pang Lee，原文括号内为彭嘉，前文为彭蠡，照实译出），C!（原文如此，可能为Commander缩写或乱码）
上海青年流动宣传团。
